short: Follow the team’s overall passing strategy more.
Standard.text: Passing directness will be driven by the team’s passing strategy, the role and personal preferences.
cons: Could benefit from a more tailored strategy.

Take more risks.text: Encourages the player to play more low-percentage passes and through balls in the hope that one or two of them will unlock the opposition defence in a potentially decisive manner.
pros: Player may be able to unlock the opposition defence more often.
Takes advantage of player’s vision and passing ability.
cons: Less patience in attack.
Higher chance of giving the ball away.

Take fewer risks.text: Asks to retain possession first and foremost, playing a sensible and patient passing game without unnecessarily conceding possession.
pros: Better chance of retaining the ball.
Feeds the ball into more creative teammates.
cons: Less chance of player progressing the ball.
Player is less likely to create chances.

Standard.text: The player’s passing risk will be driven by the team’s passing strategy, their role and their own personal preferences.
pros: Provides a balance between passing safety and risk.
cons: Could benefit from a more tailored strategy.

short: Defence has more time to react to the cross.
Aim for the opposite side of the box.
Aim for far post.text: Asks to deliver crosses towards the far post when possible.
pros: Far post tends to have less defensive coverage.

short: Aim for the middle of the box.
Aim for centre.text: Asks to deliver crosses towards the middle of the box when possible.
pros: Largest margin for error.
cons: Easier for goalkeeper to claim the ball.

short: Aim for the near side of the box.
Aim for near post.text: Asks to deliver crosses towards the near post when possible.
cons: Chance of not beating the first defender.
Reliant on target forward being able to win their duels.

short: Aim for the team’s target forward.
Aim for target forward.text: Asks the player to deliver their crosses towards the team’s target forward, if there is one.
pros: Crosses towards the team’s best aerial threat.
cons: Reliant on target forward being able to win their duels.

Standard.text: Free to choose the best area to cross the ball into based on the situation.
pros: Free to choose the best type of cross.
cons: Could benefit from a more tailored strategy.

Cross from deep.text: Asks to cross the ball into the box as soon as they get the opportunity to do so, rather than try to work the ball into a better area beforehand.
pros: Gets crosses into the box more often.
cons: Crosses are made from lower quality positions.

Cross from byline.text: Asks to get the ball as high up the pitch as possible in wide areas before attempting to cross the ball into the penalty area.
pros: Crosses are made from higher quality positions.
cons: Gets crosses into the box less often.

short: Crossing frequency will be driven by playing style and personal preference.
pros: Follow the team’s overall crossing strategy more.
cons: Could benefit from a more tailored strategy.

More often.text: Asks the player to be more proactive when it comes to pressing, looking to engage the opponent more often when an opportunity presents itself.
pros: Higher chance of forcing opposition errors.
Puts more pressure on the opposition ball-carrier.
cons: Increases the amount of running the player has to do.
Easier to be dragged out of position.

Less often.text: Asks to be more patient when it comes to pressing, waiting more for the right opportunity to engage with the opponent.
pros: Conserves more energy.
Harder to be dragged out of position.
cons: Less chance of forcing opposition errors.
Puts less pressure on the opposition ball-carrier.

Standard.text: Player will follow the team’s overall pressing strategy more.
cons: Could benefit from a more tailored strategy.

Mark tighter.text: Ask the player to stick particularly tight to their mark in defensive situations in order to limit the space they have to attack the ball.
pros: Puts more pressure on the opposition.
Allows the player to use their physicality more.
cons: Easier to get drawn out of position.
Could get turned by faster and more agile opponents.

Standard.text: The player’s marking distances will be driven by the team’s defensive strategy, their role and their own preferences.
pros: Allows the player to decide their best approach.
A balanced marking strategy.
cons: Doesn’t make as much use of the player’s physicality.
May allow the opposition more space.

Tackle harder.text: Encourages the player to be aggressive and engage their mark as much as possible, using their physicality and putting in tackles in order to win the ball back.
pros: Proactive defending can stop an attack earlier.
Can unsettle the opposition.
cons: Higher risk of giving away free kicks.
Player can more easily be drawn out of position.

Ease off tackles.text: Encourages the player to stand their ground more when their mark receives the ball, instead looking to stay goal side and shield them away from danger.
pros: Lower risk of giving away free kicks.
Player doesn’t get drawn out of position as much.
cons: Less chance of stopping attacks at source.
Allows the opposition more time on the ball.

Standard.text: The player’s tackling and engagement will be driven by the team’s defensive strategy, their role and their own preferences.
pros: Follows the team’s tackling strategy.
Allows the player to decide their best approach.
cons: Could benefit from a more tailored strategy.

short: Allows you to target the opposition's key creative threat.
Mark specific player.text: Asks to closely follow a specific opposition player around the pitch, in an effort to mark them out of the game. This instruction only applies to open play situations, so does not affect how the player marks during set pieces.
pros: Ensures that the chosen player is always being marked.
cons: Could be vulnerable if mark interchanges positions with their teammates.
Player can easily be dragged away from their position.

Mark specific position.text: Asks to closely follow any opposition player playing in the selected position, in an effort to mark them out of the game. This instruction only applies to open play situations, so does not affect how the player marks during set pieces.
pros: Allows you to target a key position in the opposition’s attacking system.
Ensures that the chosen position is always being marked.
cons: Could be vulnerable against teams with fluid attacking systems where defined positions are less clear.
Player can easily be dragged away from their position.

Standard.text: The player will mark in a way that best suits the team’s overall defensive strategy.
pros: Allows the player to decide the best player to mark based on the situation.
Fits in to the team’s overall marking structure.
cons: Could benefit from a more tailored strategy.

short: Attack the middle of the penalty area.
Centre.text: Instruct the player to look to attack middle of the box when the ball is in a wide attacking position.
pros: Best shooting position.
In position to react to rebounds or loose balls.
cons: Higher chance of goalkeeper claiming a cross aimed at this area.
Middle of the box is often more congested.

short: Attack the left side of the penalty area.
Left.text: Encourage the player to look to attack the left side of the penalty area where possible.

short: Attack the right side of the penalty area.
Right.text: Encourage the player to look to attack the right side of the penalty area where possible.
pros: Allow others to attack the middle of the box.
Harder for goalkeeper to intercept crosses aimed there.
cons: Chance is from a tighter angle.

short: Attack the side of the box that is closer to the ball.
Near post.text: Instruct the player to look to attack towards the near side of the box when the ball is in a wide attacking position.
pros: Less opportunity for defenders to intervene.
Draw defenders away for teammates to have space to take advantage of.
cons: Chance will often be from a tight angle.
Timing of run is critical.

short: Attack the side of the box that is further from the ball.
Far post.text: Instruct the player to look to attack towards the far side of the box when the ball is in a wide attacking position.
pros: Exploits the blind side of defenders.
Goalkeeper is unlikely to be able to claim a cross aimed at the far post.
cons: More chance for defenders to intervene.
Relies on a physical advantage against the opposition’s far-side defender.

pros: Player moves into areas they feel best suits them based on the situation.
cons: Could benefit more from a tailored strategy.

Attack defensive line.text: Instruct the player to try to engage the defensive line with their movements inside the box.
pros: Well-timed runs can lead to excellent scoring opportunities.
Opens up space for teammates behind them to exploit.
cons: Have to contest more with opposition defenders.
Role is more physically demanding.

short: Position in space in front of the defensive line.
Arrive from deep.text: Instruct the player to try and exploit the space in front of the opposition defensive line.
pros: Creates separation from defenders.
In position to receive pull-backs from teammates.
cons: Positions themselves further away from goal.
Can be nullified if opposition midfielders track their run.

Standard.text: The player’s attacking movement inside the box will be driven by their role and their own personal preference.
pros: Player moves into areas they feel best suits them based on the situation.
cons: Could benefit more from a tailored strategy.

warnings.696121: The team should not use {a role} when there is an attacking midfielder positioned further ahead as this role looks to move forward into an attacking midfield position, which is already occupied.

warnings.696126: We could benefit from using a combination of Stopping and Covering roles in central defence.
warnings.696127: The team has too many players in outlet roles, which could leave us short defensively.
warnings.696128: The team has too many players in Screening or Holding roles, which will impact our ability to press the ball higher up the pitch because we'll be short on numbers.
warnings.696129: We have too many pressing roles in the team, which leaves us short on numbers at the back. By over-committing to the press, we risk being exposed by direct passes.

warnings.696133: We would recommend only having one wide covering midfielder in the current setup. By having too many, we risk leaving central areas of the pitch too exposed defensively.
warnings.707738: Asking our only defensive midfielder to press is a risky strategy as it'll leave a big gap in midfield for the opposition to exploit.
